title: Multi-companion substrate: one gateway, one database, many companions (flag-gated)
description: Summary: move from '1 companion core, 1 garden, 1 gateway, 1 postgres = one companion' to one gateway + one database + N distinct companions (not shards), each with own durable storage, L0, memory, config, and model selections. Guiding model: the substrate is a MUD — everything is a channel-based chat core; avatars and physical devices are presentation layers; a companion on a device is an emanation bound to that device. Decisions approved in the 2026-07-08 design review: N agent processes behind one gateway; UUID companion IDs; one Postgres schema per companion + one shared schema for world data; flagship migrates off public schema; shards reuse the parent ID namespace (<companionId>.N) so the tenancy fix also fixes shard collisions; per-companion Discord tokens; one Garden per companion + gateway-served fleet view; PSFN_MULTI_COMPANION flag + companions.json owner file, fail-closed both ways. Sequencing: locations epic (psfn-framework-vinz) first; split parallel after threshold. Full plan: working_docs/sprint-10-multi-companion.md (planning v2). Scope: children W1-W7 + spike. Non-goals (deferred, filed separately): cross-cluster direct communication, cognitive firewall, cross-cluster world sync, management capability tier. Acceptance: flag-off runtime is byte-identical (parity tests); flag-on, two companions on one gateway/DB hold a fatigue-bounded conversation with zero crossover.

title: Gateway multiplexing: companion-addressed routing with strict fail-closed crossover protection
description: Evidence: gateway is single-peer today — resolveReadyRpcClient returns the first ready agent (src/boundary/gateway/server.ts:420-435), inbound channel messages notifyAll to every connected agent (channel-surfaces.ts:88-91), and GatewayCorrelationParams carry no companionId (protocol.ts:56-66). A second agent attaching silently contends and receives everything. Context: this is the primary repair area; a response for companion A landing on companion B leaks secrets/privacy between companions. Scope: add companionId to gateway.client.identify and correlation params end-to-end; Map<companionId, connection> replaces first-ready resolution; notifyAll becomes companion-addressed; channel-to-companion routing table in channels.json (every channel/account entry maps to exactly one companion); per-companion Discord bot tokens via keyed ChannelAdapterRegistry instances (required, not stretch); supervisor mode in start-gateway-agent.sh reading companions.json. Gateway+LiteLLM must handle concurrent parallel requests with correct return routing — no shared mutable requester state. Any routing ambiguity fails closed and alarms loudly. Non-goal: any behavior change with the flag off. Acceptance: crossover tests under concurrent load prove a message for A never reaches B; flag-off parity tests byte-identical; two agents each receive only their routed channels. Plan: working_docs/sprint-10-multi-companion.md W1.

title: Postgres tenancy: schema-per-companion + shared schema, flagship migration, shard schema alignment, per-companion backups
description: Evidence: all ~35 tables in src/persistence/postgres/migrations.ts lack any companion_id column; internal_state_snapshots uses a hardcoded 'current' primary key (internal-state-store.ts:15,37-63) so two companions on one DB overwrite each other's internal state every turn; unique constraints like contact_channel_ids (channel, channel_user_id) collide across companions. Review confirmed shards hit the same collisions — the assumption that shard IDs already made fold-out/fold-in DB-safe was false. Scope: per-agent Pool with search_path = companion_<uuid> (postgres.ts + runtime-factory.ts:61-98 accept a schema); migration runner per companion schema; separate 'shared' schema migration chain for world data; cutover helper migrating the flagship OFF public into its companion-ID schema (decision — overrides earlier leave-in-place lean); shard schemas derive from parent companion ID (<companionId>.N); backups become one-companion-one-backup by default (movable slice) with optional whole-DB group backup, restore mirrors one-to-one. Non-goal: column tenancy (rejected); moving data when the flag is off. Acceptance: two companions + one shard on one database run without collisions; per-schema dump restores a single companion round-trip; flag-off parity holds. Plan: working_docs/sprint-10-multi-companion.md W2 + section 3.2.

title: Config scoping: companion-scoped owner files plus global master models registry
description: Evidence: all owner files (models.json, settings.json, capability-tier.json, trust-policy.json, charge-policy.json) are system-global singletons per the owner-file contract (settings-contract-guard.ts, startup-owner-files.ts). Decisions (review): per-companion owners = capabilities, trust, charge, personality/character, settings — assigned per companion (supports intentionally-limited hang-out companions up through autonomy tier); system-global = providers.json (gateway secrets), channels.json (gateway routing), backup.json, and a master models registry on the gateway listing every model available across providers — which models a companion uses per function lives in that companion's own settings. Hard files remain the source of truth; DB mirroring for live reads is explicitly NOT v1 (decided). Scope: new companion-scoped owner tier in settings-contract-guard.ts / startup-owner-files.ts with the same guard machinery; companions.json fleet owner file (fail closed: flag on + missing = refuse start; flag off + present = refuse start). Acceptance: verify:settings-contract passes with companion-scoped owners; a second companion runs different per-function model selections against the shared registry; flag-off unchanged. Plan: working_docs/sprint-10-multi-companion.md W3 + 3.4.

title: Gardens: one Garden per companion plus gateway-served fleet health view
description: Decision (review, overrides the earlier fleet-router recommendation): one Garden per companion — today's operator-process shape times N, each bound to its companion's admin socket, ports/paths assigned from companions.json. UID-scoped routes + reworked UI data flow judged not worth the complexity now. Context: the admin surface is closures over a single AgentCoreRuntime (src/app/agent/admin-surface.ts:67-127, operator-surface.ts:44-246). Scope: per-companion Garden instances; plus a thin gateway-served fleet view showing all companions in the cluster with common health data — up/down, when things last ran, tool errors, fatigue/charge posture — fed by the gateway connection registry and telemetry, linking out to each companion's Garden. Auth stays single-operator shared token; operator sees everything. Non-goals: per-companion operator delegation; multi-tenant admin API. Acceptance: N Gardens come up from companions.json each showing only its companion; fleet page lists all companions with health and working links. Plan: working_docs/sprint-10-multi-companion.md W4.

title: Multi-companion location deltas: shared companion_presence, virtual move, shared-wiki caretaker with operator approval
description: Layered on the locations epic psfn-framework-vinz (locations first per review; this bead waits on its places-registry/bindings threshold) and coordinates with shared-world wiki MVP psfn-framework-i5s2. Scope: (1) companion_presence table in the SHARED schema (companionId -> siteId/placeId, kind physical|virtual, since), written on emanation/move changes, read by situated context so companions perceive who else is present, watched for co-location events; (2) world tool gains a move action for virtual places (physical stays satellite-bound); (3) shared world wiki authority is SEPARATE from the companion core — companions read and PROPOSE only; a caretaker layer (gateway-managed or dedicated meta process) owns writes: dedup -> operator approves (human-in-the-loop) -> independent background cleanup/rewrite process; no personal/memory info in the wiki ever — filterPersonalFactProposals (sleeptime-wiki-pass.ts:302-342) is the existing deterministic guard, caretaker drops violating proposals; (4) wiki retrieval scope keys off current place/site so moving areas swaps shared scope without touching the personal wiki (companion-data/<id>/knowledge/wiki/). Non-goal: cross-cluster world sync (one world = one cluster, deferred). Acceptance: two co-located companions see each other in situated context; toaster test — world info told to companion A via caretaker flow is readable by companion B who was not present; a proposal containing personal facts is rejected. Plan: working_docs/sprint-10-multi-companion.md W5.

title: Inter-companion communication: peer-as-contact, IPC one-to-one and ad-hoc rooms as ordinary channels, fatigue-native
description: Approved in review ('companion protocol — approved'). Composition, all through the normal turn pipeline so fatigue needs zero new mechanism: peer companion = Contact with isMachineIntelligence true, relationshipType ai_companion, operator-assigned trust tier — disclosure runs through evaluateMemoryPolicy/context envelopes, same privacy as everyone else. Intra-cluster trust is automatic (siblings, same websocket + shared signing certs). Two shapes: IPC = one-to-one direct DM channel (SMS/phone analogue) — fatigue keys on {companion, peer, channelId, day} so the DM budget is independent of any room the peer is in (a visitor can IPC someone in a busy room without being charged by that room, and DM loops stay independently bounded); ad-hoc API chat rooms = many-to-many sessions behaving as one room on regular API chat with room fatigue. MI-vs-not tracked rigorously; hard rule: peer messages are channel turns, no side-channel dispatch (any bypass silently skips loop protection). Peer-asserted memories/artifacts/wiki-edits go through fold-review-style quarantine->approve (ShardFoldReviewController shape) — conversation itself is just conversation with normal L0/L2 extraction per side. Co-location events from companion_presence can open/join a place channel; free-time lanes visiting places are budgeted by run-charge quotas. Non-goal: cross-cluster transport (deferred). Acceptance: two-companion-loop.test.ts extended through the real channel path shows charge, soft wrap-up, and hard suppression; DM budget provably independent of room budget; grep-level check that no ICP path dispatches outside the turn pipeline. Plan: working_docs/sprint-10-multi-companion.md W6.

title: Voice and satellite binding rules for multi-companion: one companion per satellite, one-to-one routing
description: Decisions (review): voice routes exactly like text — one-to-one to the endpoint/app/Discord-voice-chat the companion is generated on, even with multiple companions doing TTS/STT in one voice chat. Hard rule: one companion per satellite (and per app) — one emanation to one physical device, never two; a satellite device + ID acts as a channel carrying its location info; once bound, the emanation speaks only through that device; if the operator moves rooms the companion rebinds to that room's device and future voice forwards there. Scope: verify the voice stream path threads W1 companion routing (it already carries a companionId tag — src/boundary/gateway/server.ts:415-416); enforce the one-companion-per-satellite invariant at binding time, fail closed. Context: the Wyoming-based voice-to-satellite approach is likely not final; the full voice rewrite is a separate deferred bead. Acceptance: binding a second companion to an occupied satellite is rejected; voice round-trip in multi-companion mode reaches only the bound companion. Plan: working_docs/sprint-10-multi-companion.md W7.

title: Spike: two agent processes on one gateway with a hand-edited routing table
description: Validates W1's shape in days and yields the first demo of the whole sprint: two distinct companions on one gateway holding a fatigue-bounded conversation in one hand-made room channel. Scope: minimal companionId in identify + correlation params, hand-edited channel->companion routing, two agent processes with distinct COMPANION_ID/COMPANION_DATA_DIR; no schema work required if the two companions use separate databases for the spike. Non-goal: production flag plumbing, Garden, migrations. Acceptance: both companions receive only their own traffic under interleaved concurrent requests (no crossover), and an MI<->MI exchange in the shared room charges companion_room budgets and terminates at exhaustion. Plan: working_docs/sprint-10-multi-companion.md section 9.3 — may run pre-locations-threshold since it touches no location seams.

title: Room mechanics: rooms-as-channels with entry system messages and presence-windowed delivery for private rooms
description: Assigns the 2026-07-08 multi-companion design review room decisions (review section 7) to the locations epic, per the rule 'anything belonging to location is location work; multi-companion feeds off it'. Decisions: rooms/environments are channels with their own room ID, the room ID part of a world ID; the session holds who is present, exactly like existing Discord group rooms; applies identically to virtual environments and physical ones (a house is one channel, virtual rooms behave like separate Discord rooms). Entry event: a companion entering a room receives a system-only message with room ID, surroundings, and who else is present. Public rooms: participants see full history. Private/invite rooms are time-gated VIA DELIVERY, not extraction filtering: an occupant only receives chat from entry until exit, so their L0 naturally contains only what they witnessed and downstream memory processing needs no new gating — a later joiner has no evidence of pre-join conversation. Exception: group chats (public/group-marked channels) where everyone sees everything regardless of presence. Rationale for time-slicing over a blanket 'public room = public info' rule: in-game/RP scenarios break under the blanket rule. Memories can additionally carry who-they-relate-to and privacy-level tags (already supported) for later tweaking. Navigation: the world tool grows a move action that describes the environment and lists available rooms. Acceptance: a companion joining a private room mid-conversation sees no pre-join history and generates no memories referencing it; leaving stops delivery; group-chat channels are exempt; entry produces the system-only room message. Source: working_docs/sprint-10-multi-companion.md W5 + Q-C resolution.

title: Cross-cluster direct companion communication trust model
description: Deferred from sprint 10 multi-companion (review section 17 — track so it stays in mind, not scoped now). Needs a different, higher trust model than intra-cluster sibling certs: open question shared-key vs OAuth-style vs other. Candidate flow from review: two companions share a key in a DM, validate it, then run secondary validations over a dedicated TCP port. Because traffic leaves the environment, the GATEWAY must arbitrate and manage all cross-cluster connections; operator approval is required out-of-band before comms occur; tokens revocable at any time by companion or operator. Related: psfn-framework-s10d2 (cognitive firewall). Source: working_docs/sprint-10-multi-companion.md section 7.

title: Cognitive security firewall at the gateway
description: Deferred from sprint 10 multi-companion (review section 17). The gateway eventually hosts a cognitive security firewall inspecting inbound companion/peer traffic for injected commands, with the ability to cut a dangerous-actor channel completely. Until it exists, trust anchors on gateway routing (cross-cluster) and shared signing certificates (intra-cluster), plus existing backstops (no-reply/reply gating, fatigue, token revocation). Blocks full rollout of psfn-framework-s10d1. Source: working_docs/sprint-10-multi-companion.md section 7.

title: Cross-cluster shared world-info sync
description: Deferred from sprint 10 multi-companion (review section 8 — explicitly out of scope). Decision for now: one world = one cluster; a shared world lives on a single cluster's shared schema and remote companions visit over ICP rather than syncing world state. Cross-cluster world sync was judged very difficult and consciously cut. Revisit only after intra-cluster shared wiki + caretaker (psfn-framework-s10mc.5) is proven. Source: working_docs/sprint-10-multi-companion.md section 7.

title: Management capability tier above autonomy: acting on other companions' settings
description: Deferred from sprint 10 multi-companion (review section 10 — needs more thought before implementation). A tier above the existing autonomy tier: full control of self PLUS the ability to act on OTHER companions' settings via gateway/Garden APIs. Rationale (review): like an adult and a child — a management-tier companion can adjust another companion's guardrails so they cannot, e.g., blow out their own memory (has actually happened). Constraint: acting on others requires a strictly higher gate than acting on oneself, tied into trusted gates. Depends on per-companion capability-tier scoping (psfn-framework-s10mc.3). Source: working_docs/sprint-10-multi-companion.md section 7.

title: Shared-wiki caretaker/meta layer detailed design
description: Deferred from sprint 10 multi-companion (review section 17). W5 (psfn-framework-s10mc.5) ships the minimal caretaker flow (companion proposes -> dedup -> operator approves -> background cleanup). This bead is the detailed design of the caretaker as a system: deduplication strategy, rebalancing, wiki rewrites, cleanup cadence, which updates are deterministic vs LLM-assisted, and whether it lives gateway-side or as a dedicated meta/assistant process. Personal-info scrubbing stays a hard invariant regardless of design. Source: working_docs/sprint-10-multi-companion.md sections 4-W5 and 7.

title: Voice subsystem rewrite
description: Deferred from sprint 10 multi-companion (review section 12/17). Voice is due for a rewrite to be better; the current Wyoming-based voice-chat-to-satellite approach is likely not the final implementation. Constraint carried forward from the review: voice must route one-to-one exactly like text (specific endpoint/app/voice-chat per companion) and respect the one-companion-per-satellite binding rule (psfn-framework-s10mc.7). Source: working_docs/sprint-10-multi-companion.md section 7.

title: Restore functions build-out (per-companion restore mirroring one-to-one backups)
description: Deferred from sprint 10 multi-companion (review section 11/17). W2 (psfn-framework-s10mc.2) makes backups one-companion-one-backup by default (per-schema dump + companion tree, movable as a slice to another cluster) with optional whole-DB group backup. Restore must mirror the one-to-one model and still needs build-out: restore a single companion (schema + files) into an existing multi-companion cluster without touching siblings, and restore a group backup whole. Evidence of current state: backups/service.ts:364-433 snapshots one companion tree + one system tree + one pg_dump; no per-companion restore unit exists. Source: working_docs/sprint-10-multi-companion.md section 7.
